record.paper_title: Solutions to four open problems on quorum colorings of graphs
record.original_question: Does every graph G satisfy the inequality ⌊diam(G)/2⌋ ≤ ψ_q(G), where diam(G) is the graph diameter and ψ_q(G) is the quorum coloring number?

evidence.quote: Hence, we deduce that lim ℓ→+∞ diam(Gℓ) = +∞, which answers Questions 3 and 4 in negative.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple connected graph. For a vertex $v\in V$, let $N[v]=\{v\}\cup\{u\in V:uv\in E\}$ denote the closed neighborhood of $v$. A partition $\mathcal{P}=\{V_1,\dots,V_k\}$ of $V$ into nonempty classes is called a quorum coloring of $G$ if for every vertex $v\in V$, writing $V_{i(v)}$ for the class containing $v$, one has
$$|N[v]\cap V_{i(v)}|\ \ge\ 	frac{1}{2}|N[v]|.$$
The quorum coloring number $\psi_q(G)$ is the maximum number of classes $k$ over all quorum colorings $\mathcal{P}$ of $G$. Let $\mathrm{diam}(G)=\max_{u,v\in V}d(u,v)$ denote the diameter of $G$.

Decide whether the inequality
$$\left\lfloor 	frac{\mathrm{diam}(G)}{2}ightfloor\ \le\ \psi_q(G)$$
holds for every finite simple connected graph $G$. If it does not, exhibit a family of counterexamples.
artifact.status_search_result: The question was posed as an open problem on quorum colorings and has been resolved in the negative: there exists a family of graphs $G_\ell$ with $\mathrm{diam}(G_\ell)\to\infty$ for which the inequality fails, so the answer is "no".

status_evidence.snippet: Hence, we deduce that lim diam(G_ell) = +infinity, which answers Questions 3 and 4 in negative.
status_evidence.claim: The proposed inequality fails in general; a family of counterexamples with unbounded diameter is constructed.
